topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukrainian negotiators are holding talks with Trump envoys in the US today and tomorrow, signaling potential movement toward peace discussions. Russian forces reportedly liberated the settlement of Kiyanitsa in Sumy region, while Russian strikes killed at least 30 people in a bus strike on Kramatorsk; Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed over 50 in three days. Finland has sent urgent defense aid to Ukraine as Russia intensifies attacks across multiple fronts.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Iran-backed Houthi forces struck Riyadh's airport with missile strikes that killed three people, escalating fighting in the Middle East conflict. US media reports suggest Trump may be weighing military strikes against Iran before the midterm elections, though he has publicly ruled this out. Iran vows to block additional Strait of Hormuz routes, raising risks for tanker traffic, while Putin offered Russia's assistance to help end the Middle East war.
topics.T15: A Category 2 hurricane is bearing down on Florida's Gulf Coast with evacuations underway; heavy rains have triggered mudslides in Santiago, Chile, sweeping away vehicles and flooding homes and hospitals. Hurricane Simon is intensifying rapidly in the Pacific and is on track for Category 4 status this weekend, posing threats to southwestern Mexico.

topics.T04: A woman died of suspected plague in Siberia, prompting quarantine and unease in Russian cities; scientists behind the AstraZeneca COVID vaccine are reportedly rushing to develop a bubonic plague vaccine as pandemic fears grow.
topics.T05: A Brazilian Supreme Court judge issued an arrest warrant for presidential candidate Eduardo Bolsonaro weeks before the country's runoff election. Germany's far-right AfD party has taken control of a state parliament for the first time in its history, marking a significant far-right electoral breakthrough.
topics.T06: Mass protests and arrests are occurring across multiple countries: India reports mass detentions ahead of planned protests; French police used teargas and batons against student protestors with over 200 injured; Belgian students protested education costs following French unrest.
topics.T07: Iran's nuclear chief rejected US demands to curb uranium enrichment, stating Tehran will neither halt enrichment nor surrender uranium. Russia warned that France's recent nuclear-capable missile launch is a national security concern and stated it will take necessary measures to protect itself.

Italy's Foreign Ministry website is under cyberattack; Italy is checking embassy sites and pushing for EU action to identify attackers. South Korean banks and Japanese companies including Daiwa Securities and SoftBank have been targeted in recent waves of cyberattacks, some reportedly involving AI tools.

bluf: Iran-backed Houthi forces struck Riyadh's airport killing three people, marking a dangerous escalation in Middle East hostilities. Ukrainian negotiators are meeting with Trump envoys in the US today and tomorrow in what could signal movement toward peace talks, even as Russian forces advance incrementally and strike Ukrainian cities with intense bombardment. Trump is reportedly being urged by media figures to authorize military strikes on Iran before midterm elections, though he has publicly denied weighing such action. A Category 2 hurricane is bearing down on Florida with evacuations underway, while Hurricane Simon rapidly intensifies toward Category 4 status in the Pacific. Additionally, Germany's far-right AfD party has achieved control of a state parliament for the first time, and Iran's nuclear chief has explicitly rejected US demands to halt uranium enrichment.
